manual.embeddeddev.seven_segment.title: 13 Segment display
manual.embeddeddev.seven_segment.body: Seven bars plus DP. Eight GPIO labels: A B C D E F G DP. Default common cathode: high lights a segment. Sneak-use for common anode: low lights it. Power and resistors are built in. Unplugging blanks it.
manual.embeddeddev.seven_segment_codes.b:
Bits 0 to 7:
A B C D E F G DP
Cathode codes (hex)
0=3F 1=06 2=5B
3=4F 4=66 5=6D
6=7D 7=07 8=7F
9=6F Point=80
Invert all bits for common anode.
manual.embeddeddev.seven_segment_example: Wire A–DP to P1.0–7. Flash examples/seven_segment_counter.hex. It counts 0–9; odd digits light DP. RAM 30H is the digit, 31H the code. For adjacent use, configure G1. Craft eight LED modules around one circuit board.

manual.embeddeddev.ds18b20.title: 12 DS18B20 thermometer
manual.embeddeddev.ds18b20.body: Place against the measured block. Connect GPIO DQ. Use to inspect temperature and source. Range -55 to 125 °C. Resolution is 9–12 bits.
manual.embeddeddev.ds18b20_protocol.body:
Reset low for 480 us.
CCH Skip ROM
44H Convert T
BEH Read 9 bytes + CRC
Signed temperature /16.
12-bit conversion: 750 ms.
manual.embeddeddev.ds18b20_temperature.b: Mekanism heat is converted from Kelvin. Create heat levels map to 20+5*level °C; passive heat maps to 60 °C. Use the probe to see the source.

manual.embeddeddev.wire_tools.title: 2.2 Wires and posts
manual.embeddeddev.wire_tools.body: Use a coil on two terminals. Aim at the board center for Up, or a rim for its side. Posts turn or branch cables. Each span is 32 blocks. Use cutters to recover wire.
manual.embeddeddev.wire_redstone.title: 2.3 Remote redstone
manual.embeddeddev.wire_redstone.body: Place a port beside a device. Use an empty hand to set its mode and redstone face. Connect it to the board. ADC reads and DAC emits a strength from 0 to 15.

manual.embeddeddev.survival.title: 0 Survival crafting
manual.embeddeddev.survival.body: Mine silicon ore in new Overworld chunks, Y -56 to 40. Use a stone pickaxe or better. Or place sand on four sides of charcoal in a crafting table. Smelt the raw silicon to make wafers.
manual.embeddeddev.survival_assembly.bod: Mix copper, clay and redstone for two circuit boards. Wafers make the MCU and crystals. Assemble the board with an 11.0592 MHz crystal. Check the recipe book for layouts.
manual.embeddeddev.stc.title: 1 STC89C52RC
manual.embeddeddev.stc.body:
Features
MCS-51 instructions and 12T timing. 8 KB program space and 256 bytes of internal RAM. Ports P0–P3 provide eight bits each.
manual.embeddeddev.stc_memory.title: 1.1 Memory and ports
manual.embeddeddev.stc_memory.body:
CODE 0000H–1FFFH
XDATA 64 KB
P0 80H / P1 90H
P2 A0H / P3 B0H
Port latches reset to FFH. Set a latch bit before reading that pin as an input.
manual.embeddeddev.board.title: 2 System board
manual.embeddeddev.board.body:
Programming
Flash an Intel HEX file. Run or step the CPU and inspect PC, accumulator and disassembly. Stop to examine the state.
manual.embeddeddev.wiring.title: 2.1 Named terminals
manual.embeddeddev.wiring.body: Each face has four groups, G1–G4. Name and bind pins per group. Aim the coil at the corresponding connector. GPIO reads and writes. ADC and DAC carry analog redstone.
manual.embeddeddev.crystals.title: 3 Crystal oscillator
manual.embeddeddev.crystals.body:
Options in MHz
6 / 11.0592 / 12 /
22.1184 / 24
Open the board socket in the top right. Swap a crystal from inventory. Changing it pauses the CPU.
manual.embeddeddev.timing.title: 3.1 Machine cycles
manual.embeddeddev.timing.body: Default 11.0592 MHz. Each machine cycle takes 12 oscillator periods. At 20 game ticks per second the default cycle budget is frequency / 240.
manual.embeddeddev.oled.title: 4 SSD1306 OLED
manual.embeddeddev.oled.body: 128 × 64 pixels. Connect SDA and SCL. The 7-bit address is 3CH. Right-click to inspect the screen. Demo pins are P1.6 and P1.7.
manual.embeddeddev.oled_protocol.title: 4.1 OLED transfers
manual.embeddeddev.oled_protocol.body: Write address 78H. Control byte 00H precedes commands, while 40H precedes pixel data. One byte covers eight pixels in a column.
manual.embeddeddev.ds1302.title: 5 DS1302 RTC
manual.embeddeddev.ds1302.body: Connect CE, SCLK and IO. Raise CE for a transfer. Commands and data are LSB first. Calendar values use BCD. The chip has 31 bytes of RAM.
manual.embeddeddev.ds1302_registers.body:
Write/read commands
80/81 seconds (CH bit 7)
82/83 min, 84/85 hour
86/87 date, 88/89 month
8A/8B day, 8C/8D year
8E/8F WP (bit 7)
BE/BF clock burst
manual.embeddeddev.ds1302_example.title: 5.2 DS1302 example
manual.embeddeddev.ds1302_example.body: To read seconds, send 81H, release IO and read eight bits. Writes use rising edges and reads use falling edges. CH=1 halts the clock. Game time and RAM persist.
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591.title: 6 PCF8591 converter
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591.body: I²C address 48H. Sneak-use to cycle 48H–4FH. AIN0–3 map to north, east, south, west. Redstone 0–15 maps to 0–255. AOUT faces up.
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591_control.title: 6.1 PCF8591 control
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591_control.body: Bit 6 enables AOUT. Bits 5:4 select input mode, bit 2 increments the channel, and bits 1:0 select the channel. The first read byte is the previous conversion.
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591_example.title: 6.2 PCF8591 example
manual.embeddeddev.pcf8591_example.body: Write 02H to address byte 90H for AIN2. Read two bytes using 91H and use the second. Write 40H and a DAC value for redstone on AOUT.
manual.embeddeddev.button.title: 7 Button panel
manual.embeddeddev.button.body: Sneak-use to set 1–9 keys and name them. Wire each key to a GPIO. Press a key to pull it low for 10 ticks. Set its port latch bit to 1 before reading it.
manual.embeddeddev.led.title: 8 LED module
manual.embeddeddev.led.body: GPIO label LED. Write 1 to light the lamp and 0 to turn it off. SETB and CLR can be used to check the wiring.
manual.embeddeddev.sensor.title: 9 Environment sensor
manual.embeddeddev.sensor.body: SDA and SCL, address 48H. Write a register number, then read. 0 redstone, 1 sky light, 2 block light, 3 day progress in percent.
manual.embeddeddev.redstone.title: 10 Redstone connector
manual.embeddeddev.redstone.body: Place next to the board and bind redstone pins on the touching side. ADC0–7 are F000H–F007H. DAC0–7 are F010H–F017H.
manual.embeddeddev.compass.title: 11 Survey compass
manual.embeddeddev.compass.body: The needle points north. Use the compass to read your heading. Board faces use world directions. The wiring page also shows your heading.
